summary: Round r1 (restricted network): primary documents located for Nepal's constitutional economic, fiscal-federal and natural-resource provisions (Constitution 2015, Nepali text and MoLJPA English translation), the key investment statutes (FITTA 2019, PPP and Investment Act 2019, Industrial Enterprises Act 2020, Land Acquisition Act 1977, Arbitration Act 1999, National Civil Procedure Code 2017) and contract-enforcement evidence (Doing Business 2020 Nepal profile, B-READY reports and methodology, judiciary annual reports and strategic plans). No document could be downloaded, so every empirical item (contract-enforcement time and cost, court backlog) is pending. Qualitatively, the leads show that investment entry is split between the Department of Industry and the Investment Board by project size under FITTA, PPPs are channelled through IBN under the 2019 Act, and fiscal and resource powers are divided across Schedules 5-9 of the Constitution; the currently applicable land-acquisition statute must be confirmed because secondary sources disagree.

findings.claim: Constitutional provisions governing economic policy, federal finance and natural resources (article-level map)
findings.note: Requires retrieval of the authoritative Nepali text and official English translation; extract directive principles on economy, financial powers of each tier, revenue-source distribution, NNRFC mandate, natural-resource benefit sharing, property rights, and Schedules 5-9. Leads: lawcommission.gov.np content/13437; ConstitutionNet MoLJPA translation.

findings.note: Retrieve each Act and its latest amendment from lawcommission.gov.np; record date of authentication and amending Acts. Land acquisition statute in force is unresolved (see data_gaps).

findings.note: Methodological rule; English translations are unofficial except where MoLJPA-issued.

Judiciary annual reports FY2076/77-FY2081/82: caseload, disposals, pending cases by tier and age (supremecourt.gov.np yearlyreps) - download blocked.

Whether a Land Acquisition Act 2076 (2019) was enacted or the 1977 Act (as amended) remains in force - secondary sources conflict; need lawcommission.gov.np prevailing-law list.
Latest amendment status of FITTA 2019 and PPP and Investment Act 2019 (incl. any ordinance-based amendments) - need Nepal Gazette / Law Commission consolidated texts.
B-READY coverage of Nepal and Dispute Resolution scores.
Unit code for durations in days is absent from src/economic_model/units.py.

assumptions.text: Nepali statute text on lawcommission.gov.np is authoritative; English translations used only for reference.
Doing Business (discontinued) and B-READY dispute-resolution measures are treated as separate, non-comparable series; neither is spliced.
assumptions.basis_note: original label: 'assumption (methodology differs: DB used a standardised case in the largest business city; B-READY uses expert consultations and firm surveys on a different scoring framework)'

challenges.text: Assignment matrix should cite constitutional Schedules 5-9 directly from the authoritative text used by 11A, so both registers share one article-level mapping.
Any strategy relying on large land-intensive FDI/PPP projects must reference the land-acquisition statute actually in force; its status is unresolved in r1.

uncertainty: High: no primary document was retrievable in r1, so no empirical value is recorded. Main qualitative uncertainty is statutory currency (amendments and whether a newer land acquisition law replaced the 1977 Act). Contract-enforcement metrics exist only in a discontinued series (DB2020, data vintage 2019) and a methodologically different successor (B-READY), so time-series comparison is not possible. Court statistics use Nepali fiscal years (mid-July) and count caseload including carried-over cases, which must be distinguished from new filings.

constitutional_constraints.method: Article-level extraction from the authoritative Nepali text with MoLJPA English translation: directive principles on economic policy; financial powers and revenue-source distribution by tier; NNRFC mandate on revenue sharing, grants, borrowing limits and natural-resource benefit sharing; property rights and acquisition for public purpose; Schedules 5-9 exclusive and concurrent powers. Each constraint entry will cite article/schedule and observation id of the retrieved text.

enforcement_metrics.method: DB2020 Enforcing Contracts (time, cost, judicial-quality index; vintage 2019) kept separate from B-READY Dispute Resolution scores; court backlog from judiciary annual reports by BS fiscal year and tier, incl. age-of-case breakdown.

Needed for constitutional_constraints.
